title: Open the gates at Victoria Park
text: The members want a session thrown open at Victoria Park, where the old-timers say the club's soul lives. Thousands would come, the deck is rock hard and the fitness staff want a closed, sharp session.

choices.label: Open the gates

effects.hit_result: The hard deck takes it out of the legs.

choices.result: Victoria Park is packed. The session is looser than the coaches wanted.

choices.label: Train behind closed doors

effects.why: You shut the faithful out

choices.result: A full, sharp session. The faithful are left outside the fence.

title: Voted the most hated club, again
text: A radio poll has voted Collingwood the most hated club in the land again. The players heard it on the drive in.

choices.label: Let them hate us
choices.result: The line goes round the league. This week's opponent has heard it too.

choices.label: Say the club is for everyone

effects.why: The group wanted a coach who'd wear it

choices.result: A gracious answer. The rooms wanted a bit more mongrel.

title: The Colliwobbles question
text: Finals week, and the papers have dug up the old word. Every question at the press conference is whether this side will choke when it matters.

choices.label: Name the word and laugh at it
choices.result: You laugh it off on camera. If this one goes wrong, the word is back on every front page.

choices.label: Shut the questions down

effects.why: The group stayed on the job in finals week

choices.result: You won't take the question. The press say it's a sore point.

title: A legend wants to bury the curse
text: Before September starts, a club legend wants to hold a mock funeral at the old ground to bury the finals curse for good, with the cameras rolling.

choices.label: Hold the funeral
choices.result: A coffin, a brass band and a lot of laughs. If the side bombs out now, the curse is back.

choices.label: Get back to work

effects.why: Finals week stayed about the football

choices.result: No funeral. The members wanted the show.

title: Building for a flag, or treading water?
text: The biggest supporter base in the game is restless for a premiership. The board wants to know if you're building for a flag or treading water.

choices.label: Promise a crack at it now

effects.why: You promised a crack at the flag

choices.result: The board loves it. Every loss now gets measured against your promise.

choices.label: Ask for time to rebuild

effects.why: The club is building something together

effects.hit_result: A senior player asks where he fits in a rebuild.

choices.result: The board gives you time. The members are not patient people.

title: Floreat Pica above the race
text: The leadership group wants the club motto, "may the magpie flourish", above the race and the season's standards built around it.

choices.label: Back it and make it a standard

effects.why: The motto went up over the race

effects.hit_result: Some of the group find it heavy-handed.

choices.result: The motto goes up. Every player touches it on the way out.

choices.label: Leave it to the players

effects.why: The players were trusted to set their own standards
Nobody owned the standards

choices.result: The leaders run with it their own way. It drifts a bit.

title: {name} is meant to lead the song
text: {name} is new to the side, and when he gets his first win, tradition says he leads Good Old Collingwood Forever in the rooms. He's terrified.

choices.label: Make him lead it

hit.why: The new boy led the song

effects.hit_result: He belts it out and the room goes wild.
effects.miss_result: He freezes halfway through and the senior players have to carry it.

choices.result: {first} stands on the bench in the middle of the rooms.

choices.label: Let a senior player lead it
choices.result: A senior player leads it. {first} feels he missed the ritual.

title: Carlton week
text: It's Carlton, the oldest grudge in the game. Supporters stop you in the street to tell you what this one means.

choices.label: Make it the game of the season
choices.result: Training is a war all week. Lose this and it will hurt.

choices.label: Treat it as just another game

effects.why: The week ran to the plan, Carlton or not

choices.result: A normal week. The supporters can't believe it.

title: Essendon at a packed MCG
text: A packed MCG, the Bombers, the whole city watching. The players want a hard week to get up for it; the doctors want them rested.

choices.label: Train hard into it

effects.hit_result: The hard week shows in the last quarter.

choices.result: A hard, physical week on the track.

choices.label: Freshen them up
choices.result: A light week. The legs are fresh for the big day.

title: A country town wants the Pies
text: A country league begs for a visit. Half the town barracks for the Pies, and the other half wants to boo them in person.

choices.label: Send a squad

effects.hit_result: Two days on the road catch up with them.

choices.result: The town turns out in black and white, and a few in other colours.

choices.label: Send a club legend instead

effects.why: The players wanted to go

choices.result: The legend charms the town. The players wanted the trip.

title: Chasing the membership record
text: The club is chasing a new membership record. Marketing wants three players at every launch for a month.

choices.label: Put the players on the launches
choices.result: The record falls. The players are sick of shopping centres.

choices.label: Keep the players out of it
choices.result: The players train. The record push stalls short of the mark.

title: One big offer
text: The board will back one big offer to another club's out-of-contract star, but it means trimming the offers to your own out-of-contract players.

choices.label: Go big on the star

hit.why: The club landed the big name

effects.miss_result: He goes elsewhere anyway, and the board wants to know why.

effects.why: Your own players took less to fit him in

choices.result: Your own out-of-contract players get trimmed offers.

choices.label: Pay your own first

effects.why: The club looked after its own

choices.result: Your own players re-sign. The board says you left a star on the table.

title: The pokies and the suburb
text: The club's poker machine venues pay a lot of the bills. A local welfare group says they drain the very suburb the club came from, and the press want your view.

choices.label: Back the board's position

effects.why: The suburb feels the club chose the machines over it

choices.result: The board is grateful. The welfare group goes to the papers.

choices.label: Say the club ought to get out of them

effects.why: You put the suburb ahead of the takings

choices.result: Your answer leads the news. The board is furious about the money.

title: A hard look in the mirror
text: A former player has said publicly that he was racially abused inside the club during his career. The board wants the coach's voice in the response.

choices.label: Front it and apologise in full

effects.why: The club owned its past in public

choices.result: You stand up and apologise without conditions. Some on the board wanted it softer.

choices.label: Leave it to the president

hit.why: The club's response landed badly with its own players

effects.hit_result: The statement reads like lawyers wrote it. The players notice.

choices.result: The president speaks for the club.

title: Two players test positive
text: Two of your players have returned positive tests to a banned substance and will miss games whatever the club says. The club has to decide what it says publicly.

choices.label: Stand by them, support first

effects.why: The club stood by its players at their worst

choices.result: The club puts its arm around them. The press and the board want a harder line.

choices.label: Take a hard line, no excuses

effects.why: The club drew a hard line on drugs

choices.result: A blunt statement. The group feels its mates were hung out.

title: A premiership hero's son
text: A premiership hero's son is coming through the draft and can join the club his father played for. The supporters want him; the recruiters rate a different kid higher.

choices.label: Take him

effects.why: The family line in black and white goes on
The recruiters lost the kid they rated higher

choices.result: He pulls on his father's colours. The recruiters' pick goes elsewhere.

choices.label: Let him go

effects.why: The recruiters got the kid they rated highest

effects.hit_result: He's starring for a rival, and the supporters never let you forget it.

choices.result: The recruiters get their man. The supporters are filthy.

title: A Gaelic footballer wants a go
text: A Gaelic footballer from Ireland has trained with the club, and the recruiters want to sign him as a project. He's never played a game of Australian football.

choices.label: Sign him

effects.hit_result: He's pushing for a senior game within a couple of seasons.
He gets homesick and goes back to Ireland.

choices.result: He signs. A list spot goes to a man who's never bounced the ball.

choices.label: Pass, keep the spot for a local

effects.hit_result: He signs with a rival and kicks a bag against you.

choices.result: A local kid gets the spot.

title: {name} wants a long speech
text: {name} has won the club champion award and wants to dedicate it to a teammate who missed the season injured. That means a long speech the board planned to keep short.

choices.label: Let him speak

effects.why: The champion gave his night to an injured mate

choices.result: {first} speaks for ten minutes. There isn't a dry eye in the room.

choices.label: Keep to the script

effects.why: He was cut short on his own night

choices.result: A short thank-you. {first} wanted to say more.

title: The cheer squad's banner has a crack at a rival
text: The cheer squad has painted a banner having a go at another club's player. It's funny, and it's going to be all over the papers.

choices.label: Let it run

effects.why: The club backed its cheer squad

effects.hit_result: The league fines the club, and the papers have a field day.

choices.result: The players run through it laughing.

choices.label: Ask them to repaint it

effects.why: The cheer squad feel the club hung them out

choices.result: A safer banner goes up. The cheer squad are cool on the club for a month.

title: The cheer squad leader's request
text: The cheer squad's leader wants the players to come out and see the supporters before a big game. The match committee wants them in the rooms.

choices.label: Send them out
choices.result: The players go out to the fence. The Magpie Army roars.

choices.label: Keep them in the rooms
choices.result: The players stay in. The cheer squad feel snubbed.

title: The president promises the top four
text: The club president has just told a radio station that the side will make the top four. Nobody asked you first.

choices.label: Back him publicly

effects.hit_result: The side drifts outside the four, and the president's words come back on you.

choices.result: You say the president's right. Now it's your target too.

choices.label: Correct him, gently

effects.why: Expectations stayed where the coach set them

choices.result: You say the side is building. The president is not pleased.

title: Clinics in the towers
text: Locals say the club has become a corporate machine and forgotten the suburb that made it. A community group asks the players to run a footy clinic at the public housing towers.

choices.label: Run the clinic

effects.why: The players went back to where the club began

choices.result: Two hundred kids and a lot of black and white. Training is cut short.

choices.label: Send a donation instead

effects.why: The suburb wanted the players, not a cheque

choices.result: A cheque goes to the community group. The press call it a cop-out.

title: A legend wants back in
text: A premiership legend wants a job as an assistant coach. The supporters love it, and your current assistant has done nothing wrong.

choices.label: Hire the legend

effects.why: A premiership man is back at the club

effects.hit_result: He was a great player. He's a poor teacher.

choices.result: The legend is back. Your old assistant clears his desk.

choices.label: Keep your assistant

effects.why: You backed the staff who'd done the work

choices.result: Your assistant stays. The supporters and the press call it a snub.

title: A heritage guernsey for one round
text: Marketing wants a heritage guernsey for one round, with a merchandise run behind it. The traditionalists say the stripes must never change; younger fans want it.

choices.label: Wear the heritage guernsey

effects.why: The traditionalists say the stripes are not for sale

choices.result: The merchandise sells. The traditionalists write letters.

choices.label: Stay in the stripes

effects.why: The stripes stay as they always were

choices.result: Black and white, as always. Marketing loses its round.

title: {name} has torn up the reserves
text: {name} has torn up the reserves for a month. The captain thinks he's ready; the match committee wants one more week.

choices.label: Pick him
choices.result: {first} is in. A senior player is dropped and lets you know about it.

choices.label: One more week

hit.why: He thinks the club doesn't rate him

effects.hit_result: He asks his manager about a trade.

choices.result: The side stays the same. {first} goes back to the reserves.
